root_cause.text: In the 9p client’s mount-option handling (`v9fs_apply_options()`), the access-mode bits in `v9fs_session_info->flags` were ORed with user ఎంప options without first clearing the existing default access mask, so `V9FS_ACCESS_CLIENT` from `v9fs_session_init()` combined with `access=user` produced an invalid mixed access state that broke UID selection in `v9fs_fid_lookup()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch notes that after `1f3e4142c0eb`, `v9fs_apply_options()` used `|=` on flags already set by `v9fs_session_init()`, and explicitly adds `v9ses->flags &= ~V9FS_ACCESS_MASK;` when `ctx->session_opts.flags & V9FS_ACCESS_MASK` is present to “avoid mangling the setting”; the CVE description says this mixed state makes access checks match neither mode, causing `v9fs_fid_lookup()` to use `INVALID_UID` instead of `current_fsuid()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix v9fs option application so session access flags correctly override existing default access flags.
intent_record.what: In v9fs_apply_options(), a new conditional clears the V9FS_ACCESS_MASK bits from v9ses->flags when ctx->session_opts.flags contains any access-mode flags, before OR-ing in the session option flags.
intent_record.how: This ensures that session-specific access settings replace any previously established default access flags instead of being merged with them, preventing the access mode from being mangled by stale bits.

grouping_result.intent: Fix v9fs option application so session access flags correctly override existing default access flags.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes v9fs option handling so access-mode flags override the default access mask instead of being ORed together, preventing the invalid mixed access state.

candidates.rationale: This ORs parsed mount options into the existing session flags without clearing the default access mask first, allowing V9FS_ACCESS_CLIENT from session initialization to persist and combine with user-specified access bits into an invalid mixed state.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement merges mount-option access bits into the existing session flags without clearing the pre-existing default access mode first. As a result, the default V9FS_ACCESS_CLIENT set during session initialization can remain set alongside user-specified access=user, producing the invalid mixed access state described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable access-mode handling is present in the new parser, but it already clears the access mask before ORing in the selected mode: `case Opt_access:` contains `session_opts->flags &= ~V9FS_ACCESS_MASK;` followed by `session_opts->flags |= V9FS_ACCESS_USER/ANY/CLIENT/SINGLE;`. That is the correct fix for the root cause described (previously ORing user options without clearing the default `V9FS_ACCESS_CLIENT`-style state). In addition, `v9fs_session_init()` now sets only the default base flag `v9ses->flags = V9FS_ACCESS_USER;` and then `v9fs_apply_options()` does `v9ses->flags |= ctx->session_opts.flags;`, but the parsed options have already had their access bits masked out first. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this commit, and the fix is already present.
